web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape—Why a Monopoly Is in Stage 4
question: Why is TSM in Weinstein Stage 4 despite 41%+ revenue growth, and what exact technical repair is required before new capital can enter?

epigraph.quote: Never argue with the tape. A great company in a Stage 4 downtrend is simply a future opportunity waiting for supply to exhaust itself.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Stage Analysis

web_blocks.text: Weekly & Daily Structure: Two-Feed Stage Reconciliation (CAP_REJECTED)

web_blocks.html: Despite strong Q3 2026 results ($46.72B sales, +41.2% YoY) and October sales (+59.7% YoY), the tape on November 13, 2026 is weak [5, 6]. TSM closed at $398.73 (-1.67% 1D, +4.77% 1W, -8.60% 1M, -7.10% 3M, +37.89% 1Y), sitting -18.20% off its $487.47 52-week high ($266.82 low) [21]. Our two technical feeds frame this pullback differently: the deterministic `facts_US_2026-11-13.json` ledger classifies TSM as Stage 1 (Basing) because $398.73 sits within -1.07% of its 200-DMA ($403.05) and holds above its $351.19 20D/63D swing low. Conversely, the TradingView/Stage 2 snapshot screen (`snapshots_US_2026-11-13.json`) flags STAGE_4 / AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN because $398.73 trails the 30-week SMA ($420.49) by -5.17% and the 50-day SMA ($430.11) by -7.30% [21]. Both feeds agree on the key gate: TSM is not in a buyable Stage 2 uptrend today (`CAP_REJECTED`) [21].

Every intermediate moving average sits overhead as resistance. The $398.73 close trails the 30-week SMA ($420.49) by -5.17%, the 10-week EMA ($414.34) by -3.77%, and the 50-day SMA ($430.11) by -7.30% [21]. It also sits -1.07% below the 200-day SMA ($403.05), clinging just above the 40-week EMA ($394.74) and 200-day EMA ($395.02) [21]. TradingView's technical rating is -0.29 (Sell), driven by a -0.67 moving-average score [21]. Meanwhile, the US market is in a 'Correction (below 50-DMA, above 200-DMA)' with 6 distribution days in 25 sessions and 52.6% breadth above the 50-DMA [28].

web_blocks.html: The 4-hour chart shows why chasing the +4.77% weekly bounce is premature. TSM closed at $398.73, still below its 4H EMA20 ($400.29) and 4H SMA50 ($413.34), with 4H RSI at 47.66 and `intraday_4h_turn: false` [21]. Volume on November 13 was 10.75M shares—just 0.79x the 30-day average (13.68M) and well under the 10-day average (17.07M) [21]. Institutional buyers are not yet stepping in to absorb overhead supply [21]. With ATR-14 at $17.10 (4.29% of price) and Bollinger Band width at 20.97%, volatility stays elevated.

The options surface offers a useful sentiment cross-check. On November 13, 2026, the CBOE total put/call ratio stood at 0.85 (equity 0.63, index 0.96) [25]. For TSM, 30-day ATM implied volatility (44.9%) trades well below 20-day realized volatility (61.9%), putting TSM in an `IV_CHEAP` regime. While `options_snapshot.py` mechanically flags a `2027-01-15 $390/$450` Bull Call Spread (`$2,373` debit = `237.3 bps` NAV, `2.55x` our `$930.80` equity stake), we do NOT recommend opening that spread today. Three flaws block it: (a) 4H repair is unconfirmed (`4H EMA20 $400.29`), (b) `2027-01-15` expires 6 days before Q4'26 earnings (~January 21, 2027) [24], and (c) `$2,373` oversizes a Correction-regime trade relative to our `1.05%` equity stake. Wait for a 4H / 30W SMA reclaim and use a post-Feb 2027 expiry if trading options.

web_blocks.title: Why Short-Term Momentum Is Avoid / Wait
paragraphs: A stock below its 50-DMA ($430.11), 200-DMA ($403.05), and 30-week SMA ($420.49) on 0.79x volume has negative short-term expectancy. Buying here means fighting trapped supply from buyers between $405 and $487 over the past four months. Wait for either a high-volume hold in $369.38–$380.64 around Pivot S1 ($375.01), or a Stage 1 base and decisive reclaim of $420.49.

web_blocks.text: Anatomy of the Overhead Supply Shelf ($403–$487)

web_blocks.html: From August to October 2026, TSM peaked at $487.47 before pulling back -18.20% [21]. That distribution left three overhead supply shelves that any rally must clear [21]. First sits the 200-day SMA ($403.05) and 20-day SMA ($408.86); second sits the 10-week EMA ($414.34) and 30-week SMA ($420.49) [21]. Third sits the 50-day SMA ($430.11) and Pivot R1 ($462.36) [21]. Until TSM exhausts sellers in $369.38–$380.64 (Pivot S1 $375.01) or reclaims $420.49 on >1.2x volume, bounces face trapped-holder selling.

TSM's 1-year return remains +37.89%, beating many cyclical peers, yet -8.60% 1-month and -7.10% 3-month returns lag Stage 2 leaders [21, 26]. By contrast, MSFT (+2.66% 1Y, -6.31% off highs) holds above its rising 30-week SMA at $460.02 [26]. In a market with 6 distribution days and 52.6% breadth above the 50-DMA, capital rotates out of extended chip winners into Stage 2 bases [28]. That rotation confirms why `CAP_REJECTED` keeps us from catching a falling knife.

web_blocks.text: What a Confirmed Stage 1 Base & Stage 2 Reclaim Looks Like

web_blocks.html: Upgrading TSM out of `CAP_REJECTED` requires one of two observable tape events [21]. (1) Support-Zone Capitulation & Reversal: price tests $369.38–$380.64 (Pivot S1 $375.01) without closing below $348.00 (below the $351.19 swing low), then prints a 4H higher low and reclaims the 4H EMA20 ($400.29) on rising volume. (2) Stage 2 Breakout: TSM bases sideways for 4–8 weeks to flatten the 10-week EMA ($414.34) and 30-week SMA ($420.49), then breaks $420.49 on >1.2x volume (>16.4M shares/day) [21].

Track these levels over the next 30 trading days: immediate resistance sits at the 4H EMA20 ($400.29) and 200-day SMA ($403.05) [21]. Higher ceilings sit at the 10-week EMA ($414.34), 30-week SMA ($420.49), and 50-day SMA ($430.11) [21]. On the downside, Pivot S1 ($375.01) anchors our $369.38–$380.64 support zone above the $351.19 swing low, $348.00 stop, and Pivot S2 ($343.89) [21].

TSM's technical posture (`STAGE_4`, `CAP_REJECTED`, 4H RSI `47.66`, Daily RSI `45.26`, volume `0.79x`) shows supply is not yet absorbed [21]. Patience at `$369.38–$380.64` or above `$420.49` remains the highest-probability play.

book_paragraphs: Chapter 7 showed that TSMC's valuation is reasonable and its peers are weaker. Chapter 8 forces an uncomfortable truth: none of that helps while the tape is unconfirmed. On November 13, 2026, TSM closed at $398.73—down 18.20% from its $487.47 high. Our market-facts ledger classifies it as Stage 1 Basing (-1.07% vs the $403.05 200-DMA, above the $351.19 swing low), while TradingView flags Stage 4 (-5.17% below the $420.49 30-week SMA and -7.30% below the $430.11 50-day SMA). Both feeds agree TSM is not a buyable Stage 2 uptrend.

Why is a company growing sales over 40% stuck in Stage 4? With the 10-year Treasury at 5.10% and the S&P 500 logging six distribution days in twenty-five sessions, funds de-gross high-beta winners first. Even after a 4.77% weekly bounce, the 4-hour chart has not turned up. TSM closed below its 4H 20-EMA ($400.29) on 10.75 million shares—just 0.79x its 30-day average—signaling a weak bounce, not institutional buying.

Consider the tape psychology between $403 and $487. Over the past three months, hundreds of millions of shares traded above $415. Buyers near the $487.47 peak now sit on an 18% drawdown. When TSM bounces 4% or 5% on light volume (10.75 million shares, 0.79x average), trapped holders use that rally to lighten risk.

That is why Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis pairs so well with fundamental research. Fundamentals tell us *what* to own; Stage Analysis tells us *when* institutional money flows our way. With TSM below its 200-day SMA ($403.05), 10-week EMA ($414.34), 30-week SMA ($420.49), and 50-day SMA ($430.11), and capped by the 4H 20-EMA ($400.29), the tide is still ebbing.

book_callouts.title: The Two Technical Paths to Action
book_callouts.text: New capital has two disciplined paths into TSM: wait for a washout holding $369.38–$380.64 around Pivot S1 ($375.01) with a $348.00 stop below the $351.19 swing low, or wait for a Stage 1 base and volume-backed reclaim of the 30-week SMA ($420.49).

book_subsections.title: Comparing TSM's Tape to Stage 2 Benchmark MSFT
paragraphs: Compare TSM's chart with Microsoft ($523.88) to see the contrast. TSM sits 5.17% below its 30-week SMA and 18.20% off its 52-week high. Microsoft sits 13.88% above its rising 30-week SMA ($460.02), just 6.31% off highs, and inside its $507.61–$526.78 Stage 2 buy zone. That is why we refuse to force new cash into TSM at $398.73.

book_subsections.title: Why Volume Dry-Up and 4H Confirmation Matter
paragraphs: In any Stage 4 correction, seller exhaustion starts with volume drying up on down days. Next come accumulation days, where price closes near session highs on 1.2x or higher volume. Today's 10.75 million shares (0.79x 30-day average) show big funds are still on the sidelines.
Waiting for either a clean defense of $369.38–$380.64 with a 4H turn, or a high-volume reclaim of $420.49, lets institutional flow do the heavy lifting first.

book_subsections.title: Technical Map for the Next 30 Days
paragraphs: Keep these exact levels written down: $403.05 at the 200-day SMA, $420.49 at the 30-week SMA, $375.01 at Pivot S1 inside our $369.38–$380.64 zone, the $351.19 swing low, and $348.00 as our hard stop. Drawing the map before the open removes emotion when volatility spikes.

book_subsections.title: Patience as a Technical Edge
paragraphs: The hardest skill in technical analysis is sitting on your hands when a great stock sits 18% off its highs. Waiting for $369.38–$380.64 or a Stage 2 reclaim above $420.49 separates disciplined compounding from catching falling knives.

book_subsections.title: How Institutional Liquidity Drives Support Tests
paragraphs: With 30-day average volume of 13.68 million shares—over $5.4 billion in daily liquidity at $398.73—TSM is one of the most liquid stocks on the NYSE. Deep liquidity means support zones like $369.38 to $380.64 around Pivot S1 ($375.01) rarely turn on a dime. Instead, large funds scale in over several sessions as selling pressure fades and 4-hour moving averages flatten.

book_subsections.title: Walking the 1W, 1D, and 4H Tape Together
paragraphs: Let us read the weekly, daily, and 4-hour charts together step by step so you and I do not guess. On the weekly 1W chart, TSM closed at $398.73. That sits 5.17% below its $420.49 30-week SMA and 3.77% below its $414.34 10-week EMA. Weekly RSI sits at 47.15, and price is testing the 40-week EMA at $394.74. That weekly structure places TSM squarely in Weinstein Stage 4 with a CAP_REJECTED timing gate.

Drop down to the daily 1D chart and you and I see the same overhead ceiling. Price failed to reclaim the 200-day SMA at $403.05 (-1.07%) and trails the 50-day SMA at $430.11 by 7.30%. Daily RSI reads 45.26, while ATR-14 sits at $17.10, or 4.29% of price. Now check the 4H intraday tape: TSM finished at $398.73, still below the 4H EMA20 at $400.29 and 4H SMA50 at $413.34. That leaves intraday_4h_turn false. Worse, volume was just 10.75 million shares, or 0.79x the 13.68 million 30-day average. Big institutions are not stepping in yet near Pivot S1 at $375.01. Until 10.75 million shares expand above the 13.68 million average on an up-close, the tape stays in repair mode.

book_subsections.title: Why Weinstein Stage 4 Demands Patience Over Heroics
paragraphs: When you and I see a +4.77% weekly bounce on 0.79x volume, the temptation is to buy early and feel clever. Resist that urge. Between August and October 2026, TSM peaked at $487.47 before sliding 18.20%. That drop trapped buyers across every shelf between $403.05 and $487.47. Whenever TSM bounces weakly into the 200-day SMA ($403.05), 10-week EMA ($414.34), or 30-week SMA ($420.49), trapped holders sell to break even.

Meanwhile, the broader US market has logged six distribution days in twenty-five sessions with 52.6% breadth above the 50-DMA. In a Correction regime, heroics get punished quickly. Patience gives you and I two clean, objective triggers instead of guesswork. We either wait for a high-volume hold in $369.38–$380.64 around Pivot S1 ($375.01) with a 4H EMA20 turn, or we wait for a Stage 2 reclaim above $420.49 on 1.2x volume. Either path lets institutional money prove demand before you and I commit fresh capital above $348.00.
